What it buys is that adding a case is one commit again instead of two, which is the cost that decides whether it earns its keep: CLAUDE.md hard rule 2 makes adding a case this repo's most common operation, every one republishes a band, and a tree only reaches count N+1 while the new case is uncommitted — so the cited row is dirty by construction, item 2 (cited-run)'s allowance permits it locally, and CI then refuses it, forcing a clean re-run, a re-citation and a second commit. PR #34 paid exactly that. The red CI run is the symptom that exposed it. From PR #32 CI run 32626835735, root-caused on `task/M32` as T-M32-13 and replayed here before this record was written. ADR-019's Ruling has said "one per (suite, environment)" since it was written; `published-band-matches-the-ledger` had no such dimension and read every `history.jsonl` row the process could see. On CI that is a strictly larger set than the committed ledger: `.github/workflows/eval.yml` runs `--suite invariant` first, that run appends its own row to the job's copy of the file, and `--suite fast` then grades ADR-019 §3's band against a ledger holding a row this machine never wrote. Red on CI, green locally, on the same tree. THE MECHANISM IS THE TIMESTAMP, NOT THE WALL CLOCK, and the first version of this record said otherwise: `evals/run.py` stamps `ts` with `time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")`, naive local time with no zone, and item 2 (cited-run)'s dirty allowance compares those strings as an ordering on real time (`r["ts"] <= ts`). A band row written on the author's laptop at `20260823-192533` is 11:25:33 UTC; CI's `invariant` row `20260823-115044` was written 25 minutes LATER and sorts eight hours EARLIER as a string. CI's row is clean — a fresh checkout makes `git_dirty()` false — so it answered yes to "was a clean row already available when this band was published?" about a moment it had not happened in, and reddened a band the allowance (PR #35 R11) exists to permit. `main` is green only because its band cites `20260823-041729`, 04:17 local, and a CI stamp sorts before that string only for a run between 00:00 and 04:17 UTC; a band republished during Taipei daytime lands in the window. A second and separate symptom rides along: CI's wall clock also enters `slowest`, which item 3 (same-ceiling) and item 4 (committed-ceiling) read — latent today at 16.03s (the rule gives 20, the committed ceiling) and ungreenable locally above 17.39s, 1.36s and 8.5% of margin against a runner spread ADR-019 §5 records at 6.8%. Every history row now carries an `env` tag (`evals/run.py` `env_tag()`: `EVAL_ENV` if set, else `ci` when the runner sets `CI` — which GitHub Actions always does, and which is what actually tags a runner — else `local`), and ADR-019 §6 item 9 (environment) filters the ledger to the band's own environment before any other item reads a row, which reaches both symptoms. It does not repair `ts`, and it is not asked to: `ts` is stamped in UTC in the same change and graded by `ledger-ts-orders-real-time`. Two properties, two fixes, neither standing in for the other — ADR-019 §7 (T-M32-13 closed on the pair). The tag is deliberately NOT derived from the effective `EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_*`, which is the obvious candidate and is wrong in exactly the case that produced the defect: CI's `invariant` ceiling is 20 and so is this laptop's, so both environments would have shared a tag on the very suite that broke. This case is driven with a synthetic ledger because the defect cannot be reproduced from the committed one — no CI row ever reaches it, which is the other half of the same root cause (T-R51, closed in ADR-019 §5/§7 by labelling CI's four numbers as hand-read values of eval-gate run 32561162459 attempts 1-4 rather than by making CI commit a row). Five things are asserted, not one: the foreign row is excluded; the SAME row measured here still reddens the band, so the filter is a filter and not a hole; an untagged row is read as `local`, which is what every row written before T-R44 is; a band naming an environment the ledger holds no rows for hits the `no_recorded_run_at` precondition instead of passing for want of anything to compare against; and two suites banded in different environments in one call do not share a filtered ledger — that last one is here because the first draft of the filter rebound `_band_wrong`'s `rows` parameter, which is invisible for as long as every published band names the same environment, and this repo publishes exactly one.

triage.note: tagged invariant and fast, like its two siblings, because the band subsystem is graded on every gate run. It costs nothing beyond `_band_wrong` on five synthetic ledgers — no ledger read, no network, no spend. What it does NOT reach, in three parts. (1) This repo publishes exactly one environment's bands (`local`), so item 9 (environment) has one environment to discriminate on here and the `ci` half of `env_tag()` is exercised by nothing but `CI=1` on a laptop (T-R74). (2) The `ts` ordering the defect actually fired through: this case grades the FILTER only. The ordering key is a separate property with a separate case (`ledger-ts-orders-real-time`). (3) These assertions use wall clocks that differ because a filter has to be shown excluding a row that would otherwise have spoken; that choice does not make wall clock the cause, and the provenance says so.
